schema: §2.7 (v0.50) -- complete per-sentence segment disposition, superseding §21 R6's not_annotatable-only shape. `not_annotatable` (R6's original array, the only key run_scoring.load_not_annotatable() reads) is preserved for scoring and holds every NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING / NOT_ANNOTATABLE / EXCLUDED span. `dispositions` is the full per-sentence record §2.7 requires, covering ANNOTATED and AMBIGUOUS spans too, which `not_annotatable` deliberately excludes -- an AMBIGUOUS span is an open reviewer question, not a settled non-item, and including it in the scoring array would resolve it silently.

reconciliation.note: 3 obligation-bearing clauses vs 1 items_annotated. 2 span(s) AMBIGUOUS, escalated per §14.3/§14.4 rather than resolved silently. Gap fully explained by recorded dispositions (nothing uncovered); resolution is a reviewer decision, not taken here.

dispositions.rule: §2.6 (§2's ‘no obligation-bearing sentences’ exclusion row, applied at sentence granularity)
dispositions.reason: A numbered/lettered section or clause heading: no subject, no modal, no clause content of any kind -- one of the 13 spans §2.7 bulk-dispositions as a single class.

dispositions.span_text: The Company and RGHI will use all commercially reasonable efforts to obtain within 24 months following the Commencement Date, from the counterparty to each Multi-party Contract any needed consent to separate the portion of such contract that relates to the goods or services purchased from or supplied to the Business under such Multi-party Contract (including but not limited to assignment or partial assignment of such contracts to the Company or RGHI or its Affiliates).

The contract constituting the separated portion of any Multi-party Contract that relates to the Business as described in the preceding sentence shall be assumed by and become the responsibility of the Company.
dispositions.rule: live rule boundary, OPEN — SPLITTING_EXCLUSION_INVESTIGATION.md Decision 4
dispositions.reason: Surplus clause #6 -- 'The contract constituting the separated portion ... shall be assumed by and become the responsibility of the Company.' A genuine two-way boundary between two established rules, not a gap in either: marked AMBIGUOUS by the cold annotator with both readings written out; gold left no trace at all.

readings.detail: An explicit by-agent exists ('by ... the Company'), so this is NOT the ABSENT-obligor branch of §3.5.3 -- a passive clause with a named by-agent is an obligation under that section's own rule.

readings.reading: §8.8 copular-status class (excluded, or 2 items under a different split)
readings.detail: 'shall be assumed by and become the responsibility of' reads as a copular status/characterisation of the contract's disposition rather than an action-verb duty -- under this reading the segment yields 2 items via a different split than the one that would follow from the first reading.

dispositions.span_text: Each Party making purchases or receiving services under any Multi-party Contract shall indemnify and hold harmless the other Party and its Affiliates for any claims, damages, etc. arising out of such purchases or receipt of services.
dispositions.rule: no identifiable exclusion rule; gold's own notes classify but never dispose it — SPLITTING_EXCLUSION_INVESTIGATION.md Category A, row 7
dispositions.reason: Surplus clause #7 -- 'Each Party making purchases ... shall indemnify and hold harmless the other Party ...'. This is §2.7's OWN worked example of 'a classification is not a disposition': C17-02's annotator_notes name this sentence 'a section 8.4 mutual case' and stop, without ever annotating or excluding it.

readings.detail: 'Each Party ... the other Party' makes the co-obligor the obligee -- the identical pattern this segment's own C17-01 (in C17-021) and C17-02 (this segment) already apply; tag mutual_obligation, annotate one direction. Strongly looks like a drafting-time omission rather than a considered exclusion.
Classified but never resolved on record; the investigation found no §2 row that would exclude it.
